h: Holy Speech Restores Delight by Rejoining Its Root

p: From the wording of the Tikkunim (Tikkun 21)
וְהָרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (עֵקֶב, חֵלֶק ג רעג, א)
it is implied that one branches off from the other,
because of the sameness of the letters in both.
are in 231 gates, forward and backward,
and as a sign for this:
"There is nothing in good higher than oneg,
and nothing in evil lower than nega";
that oneg is the acronym of
(as written in the holy Zohar cited above),
which is "and a river goes out of Eden
This is according to what is written
that flows and goes out of Eden."
And this is Yaakov Avinu, peace be upon him,
that runs from end to end"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
and he is the whole middle line,
a chariot for the attribute of Tiferes.
And truth and peace are bound to one another,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג יב, ב)
And it goes out of Eden,
שֶׁהוּא עַיִן לֹא רָאָתָה (יְשַׁעְיָה סד, ג)
as they said in the Gemara (Berachos 34b),
the intellect hidden from all thought.
for Eden shines and goes forth
for the last attribute is called "sea,"
and it is the lower wisdom,
and this is "He founded it upon seas."
And when it begins with nun, which is nahar, river,
for the nations too are called seas,
"like the roaring of the seas they roar,"
"the mighty and abundant waters of the River,
and there are the presumptuous waters,
And when it begins with nun,
that does not go out of Eden
and is not bound to the root,
then it corrupts the letters gimmel-ayin,
וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג מו, ב)
And this is what is written in the holy Zohar (III 46b):
וַיִּפַּח בְּאַפָּיו נִשְׁמַת חַיִּים (בְּרֵאשִׁית ב, ז) וְכוּלֵּי
"'And He blew into his nostrils the soul of life' (Bereishis 2:7), etc.,
And life comes from the Mazala,
and this is what ascends above
and speaks before the holy King, etc.;
and therefore it is called a speaking spirit."
And this is as we said,
it is written, "and speaking a word" (Yeshayahu 58:13),
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר חֵלֶק א לב, א)
for on Shabbos the daughter is crowned with the Avos,
is translated in the Targum "a speaking spirit."
וּכְתִיב שׁוֹמֵר פִּיו וּלְשׁוֹנוֹ (מִשְׁלֵי כא, כג)
and it is written, 'One who guards his mouth and his tongue' (Mishlei 21:23);
departs from him and goes up,
and is not able to speak;
For nega'im come because of lashon hara,
as they said (in the Gemara, Arachin 16a, and the Midrash);
and then "I was silent from good,"
is that he again merits words of Torah.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּמִדְרַשׁ רַבָּה (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה טו, ד)
And this is what they said in Midrash Rabbah (Vayikra Rabbah 15:4):
to eat and to drink and to rejoice."
Eating and drinking is in words of Torah,
and drink of the wine I have mixed,"
which is the bread of the Written Torah
and the wine of the Oral Torah
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא, חֵלֶק ג רעא, ב)
(as written in the Ra'aya Mehemna, III 271b);
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (קֹהֶלֶת רַבָּה ב, כד)
and as they said in the Midrash (Koheles Rabbah 2:24):
the verse speaks of refers to Torah and good deeds,"
and the verse would not tell
rather it refers to eating and drinking
and rejoicing in words of Torah.
And this is "to eat and to drink and to rejoice"
And this is what it says (Tehillim 32:10),
"But one who trusts in Hashem, kindness surrounds him":
he will merit words of Torah,
